links.comparator_used: Radiologists interpreted all chest radiographs without DLD (full radiologist reading/no worklist reduction).
links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity for positive outpatient chest radiograph findings in a simulated 50% worklist reduction where the lower half by DLD probability score was regarded as negative and the remaining radiographs were read with DLD by radiologists.
links.effect: Sensitivity was 82.6% (195 of 236; 95% CI: 77.5%, 87.3%) with all radiographs read without DLD versus 83.5% (197 of 236; 95% CI: 78.8%, 88.1%) in the 50% worklist reduction scenario; difference 0.8% (95% CI: - 3.8%, 5.5%), noninferiority p = 0.01. Specificity increased from 86.7% (1498 of 1728) to 90.4% (1562 of 1728), p < 0.001.
links.tradeoff: Legal responsibility for incorrect diagnoses based on AI-standalone interpretation remains an issue.
links.quote: The sensitivity was 82.6% (195 of 236; 95% CI: 77.5%, 87.3%) when readers interpreted all chest radiographs without DLD and 83.5% (197 of 236; 95% CI: 78.8%, 88.1%) in the 50% worklist reduction scenario.

design_hint: AI-based triage worklist reduction (threshold selection for autonomous negative reads)
